fields.Name: ORD-09 - Intercompany Balancing
fields.Description: The INTERCOMPANY half of the cash leg (IC1-IC12, D13). The payment-ledger bundle proved the cash leg thoroughly using only SINGLE-COMPANY orders, and that blind spot hid a real correctness bug: cash collected by company A against a line owned by company B credited A's receivable and left B's outstanding, misstating both books with nothing reconciling them. Nothing caught it because the entry BALANCED, which is the defining property of this area - every wrong answer is a balanced, posted, plausible-looking entry. These checks therefore assert WHOSE books each amount landed on, not merely that the ledger foots. Covers one entry per (payment line x company), the collector's Dr Cash / Cr own AR / Cr Due To shape, the counterparty's Dr Due From / Cr its own AR, per-company AR reconciliation, pro-rated partial payments, line-level targeting, a shared-services collector owning no line, mirrored refunds, allocation idempotency, and one payment split across two orders with different company mixes.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: A two-company order books one journal entry per company; the collector debits Cash for the gross, credits only its OWN share of AR, and credits a separate Due To line per counterparty; each other company debits Due From and credits ITS OWN AR; AR nets to zero for each company separately; a missing IntercompanyAccountMatch refuses the allocation rather than defaulting to any account; partial payments pro-rate across companies; a refund mirrors every leg on every company with all amounts positive; re-saving an allocation does not double the Due To.
